key_insight: A PT-symmetric altermagnetic topological-insulator heterostructure can produce a pure spin bulk photovoltaic effect, yielding dc spin current with no charge current when the Néel vector lies in the xy-plane.
engineering_relevance: This offers a symmetry-tunable route to light-driven spin-current generation for spintronic devices, with topology and magnetic orientation providing direct control over output type.
method: Built a 2D topological-insulator/d-wave altermagnet heterostructure with PT-symmetric degenerate bands.
Developed a non-Abelian spin BPVE theory for PT-degenerate manifolds.
Analyzed how Néel-vector orientation changes the topological phase and nonlinear optical response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports symmetry-based theoretical analysis showing that C2z symmetry suppresses second-order charge photocurrents while finite spin photocurrents remain, including sign reversals tied to local Dirac-mass changes.
watch_item: The result is symmetry- and orientation-sensitive, so practical implementation will depend on precise control of the Néel vector and preservation of the required crystalline symmetries.
paper_title: Pure Spin Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in an Altermagnetic Higher-Order Topological Insulator
